headline: Oklahoma has one big-league team. Dress the whole state in Thunder blue, under $100.
thesis: Apart from the Hornets' 2005-07 Katrina stay, the Thunder are the only big-league team Oklahoma has ever had. The market is the whole state: Tulsa, Norman, Lawton, Stillwater, tribal nations and small-town gyms. In a house split between Sooners and Cowboys, Thunder blue is the one color everyone shares, so every piece starts blue, the City Edition included. Fans are proud of a 2025 title and a roster Sam Presti drafted and developed, led by back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. A seven-game West finals loss to San Antonio still stings. Win with a deep 'Oklahoma' layer under $100 in big-box and mall doors statewide. Add a few credited, paid artist drops from the Plaza, Paseo, Deep Deuce and Tulsa, and a blue-bodied 2027-28 City Edition with 'Oklahoma' across the chest.

archetype.name: The One-Team State
archetype.description: A whole state that adopted a franchise in 2008 and now wears a champion as its civic uniform. Loud, loyal, value-minded and allergic to flash the team has not earned.

pulse.teamMoment: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is a back-to-back MVP, and his Thunder went 64-18 before San Antonio beat them 4-3 in the West finals. They're 2026-27 co-title favorites, with a BetMGM win total of 60.5, the West's highest. Luguentz Dort went to Atlanta, and Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins were traded too. In came draft picks Aday Mara (No. 12), Bennett Stirtz and Otega Oweh. Presti is keeping a payroll near $260M rather than cutting it.
pulse.sentiment: Confident but stung. Fans expect a title and see the Oct 20 opener at San Antonio as a grudge match. They trust Presti and Mark Daigneault's patient build, even as familiar rotation players leave.

topInsights.title: The market is Oklahoma, not OKC
topInsights.insight: There's no NFL, MLB or NHL team in the state. Thunder fans drive in from Tulsa, Lawton, Norman and Stillwater, and they shop big-box and mall doors along I-35, I-40 and the Turner Turnpike. The state outline and the word 'Oklahoma' travel everywhere. Area codes don't: 405 is the OKC metro, 918 is Tulsa, and 580 covers the west and south.
topInsights.implication: Lead the statewide line with the state outline and an 'Oklahoma' wordmark. Sell 405, 918 and 580 as a matched area-code set, aimed door by door. Give Tulsa (Utica Square, Woodland Hills) its own allocation.

topInsights.title: Thunder blue keeps the peace in a Sooner-and-Cowboy house
topInsights.insight: Fall closets run OU crimson and OSU orange, plenty of households are split, and everyone is Thunder. Orange-heavy or crimson-leaning blocking reads as a college pick. A burnt-orange body reads as Texas.
topInsights.implication: Make every Thunder piece blue-bodied, the City Edition included, with Sunset (#EF3B24) and red-clay rust as trim. Launch midweek or on Thunder Cup Fridays, never on football Saturdays.

topInsights.title: Red Dirt is a Stillwater sound and a Stockyards wardrobe
topInsights.insight: Red Dirt music grew out of Stillwater's songwriter scene, and Turnpike Troubadours and John Moreland carry it now. Its look lives on gig posters for rooms like Tulsa's Cain's Ballroom and in Stockyards City stores like Langston's. The clay itself stains every sneaker in the state.
topInsights.implication: Make a rust (#A8442A) and canvas capsule with gig-poster lettering by a commissioned Oklahoma poster artist. Launch it at a show booked by a Red Dirt venue. Always sell it next to a hoops-first blue line, so the Thunder never read as a country brand.

topInsights.title: Own the sky through Oklahoma landmarks, not gradients
topInsights.insight: Storm fronts and sunsets are real here, but a sky gradient alone could be Kansas City or Denver. The Thunder palette is already a sunset. Only Oklahoma has the Skydance Bridge's scissortail sail over I-40, the Deco rooflines of downtown Tulsa and OKC, and the flat sky-blue field of the state flag.
topInsights.implication: Make the Skydance sail line and stepped Deco silhouettes the signature graphics. Keep packable shells core from October to April. Hold any gradient headline until the earlier City Editions are checked, and never use tornado-damage or memorial imagery.

topInsights.title: Homegrown pride, Gilgeous-Alexander style
topInsights.insight: Fans are proudest of a core Presti drafted and developed (Williams, Holmgren, now Mara) and of Loud City at Paycom Center. They don't want a victory lap. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, from Hamilton, Ontario, is one of the league's most-watched tunnel dressers, with a Canadian following of his own.
topInsights.implication: Write opener and season copy about development and Loud City, not revenge for a loss. Keep any 2025 champion reference to licensed marks. Add a Gilgeous-Alexander tunnel-fit story once the brand and licensing path for his product is confirmed.

topInsights.title: Value-minded ritual buyers with a hard $100 line
topInsights.insight: Oklahomans buy in person: Penn Square, Academy, Dick's, Hibbett, the arena store and the Nike Factory Store at OKC Outlets on I-40. An August sales-tax holiday on clothing and shoes under $100 lands on school start. Nike has no community or flagship door in town.
topInsights.implication: Price a full Thunder ladder of tees, shorts, hoodies and youth footwear at $99 or less, with deep youth sizes. Tell the story in borrowed venues: the arena, Plaza and Midtown pop-ups, local gyms.

topInsights.title: The richest stories belong to specific communities
topInsights.insight: The state's deepest design sources are its communities. They include dozens of sovereign Native nations, Deep Deuce jazz and Clara Luper's 1958 sit-ins, and Tulsa's Greenwood and Black Wall Street. There's also the Classen Asian District, Southside car culture and the NW 39th Gayborhood. None of them is a theme to borrow, and even a name like 'Red Earth' already belongs to a Native institution.
topInsights.implication: Any piece drawing on these communities starts with a named partner. The partner sets terms, approves the work, is credited and paid, and launches it at a community event. No regalia, sacred imagery, scripts or memorial imagery.

opportunities.how: Pull existing Fall 2026 blue pieces forward. Add Loud City and Built Here copy on shelves and social. Seed watch parties with towels and tees, and stay clear of Red River Rivalry weekend.

collection.name: Clay & Sky
collection.story: Oklahoma is red clay underfoot and a huge sky overhead, and Thunder blue holds the two together. The collection runs from Stockyards work-wear to the Skydance Bridge sail line. It pairs a statewide value layer any family can afford with limited pieces by local artists.

themes.name: Red Dirt
themes.story: Stillwater songwriters, Tulsa gig posters and Stockyards work-wear, in a washed clay tone kept browner than OU crimson. Honest materials and plain type, no rhinestones.
themes.segment: Young creatives and Okie-pride lifestyle buyers
themes.graphics: A gig-poster back print of home dates by a commissioned Oklahoma poster artist. Condensed block type in distressed ink, with a small brand-style Thunder mark.
themes.materials: Garment-dyed heavyweight fleece, washed duck canvas, pearl-snap plackets, yoke seams, tooled-leather basket-weave emboss on patches.

themes.name: Skydance
themes.story: The sky, made Oklahoman: the Skydance Bridge's scissortail sail, stepped Deco rooflines from Tulsa and downtown OKC, and Dark Blue storm light. Cut for wind from October to April.
themes.segment: Game-night fans, statewide commuters and the downtown crowd
themes.graphics: The Skydance sail line as a sleeve and yoke stripe, stepped Deco skyline silhouettes, and wind-line jacquard instead of lightning bolts. Gradients appear only as a secondary lining effect.
themes.materials: Packable ripstop nylon, wind-resistant shell fabric, jacquard knits, reflective trim.

Stepped Tulsa and OKC rooflines under a Thunder-blue sky.
Directional wind-line jacquard, reflective Thunder mark.
Lightweight mesh with the sail line across the shoulders for playoffs and summer runs.

themes.story: Limited releases co-designed by paid, credited artists from the Paseo, the Plaza, Deep Deuce and Northeast OKC, and later the Asian District. Each one flips the Thunder colors instead of inventing a rival identity.
themes.segment: Collectors, the arts crowd and the communities each release comes from

pieces.detail: Artist name and district on the hem label, numbered run.
Back print by the district artist, released at a community event.
A low-price entry, with a share of proceeds directed by the community partner.

uniform.narrative: Every Oklahoman knows the line where red clay meets a storm sky. This set puts it on a Dark Blue jersey, with a rust horizon band and 'Oklahoma' across the chest drawn by Oklahoma sign painters. It targets 2027-28 because the 2026-27 set isn't confirmed yet. The state's last City Edition was a recolor, so this one gives fans an original story to collect.
motifs: A rust horizon band across the chest and yoke, with clay below and Dark Blue sky above
The Skydance Bridge sail line on the side panels
Stepped Art Deco geometry from downtown Tulsa and OKC
Directional wind lines in place of lightning bolts
Hand-painted ghost-sign texture inside the numbers
uniform.typography: An original 'Oklahoma' chest wordmark in Route 66 and Automobile Alley showroom lettering, hand-drawn by a commissioned Oklahoma sign painter. The Utah Jazz and Indiana Pacers set the state-name precedent. Numbers are outlined slabs in Yellow with a rust keyline. Get the league's read on the wordmark at concept stage.
details: Waistband: wind-line jacquard in Dark Blue and rust
Neck tape: Thunder Up in small block type
Jock tag: the sign painter's credit
Shorts: state silhouette on the leg panel
Court tie-in: Dark Blue floor with a red-clay apron and the state silhouette at center
avoid: Native regalia, tribal patterns, the Osage shield on the state flag, or names such as 'Red Earth' that belong to Native institutions
Land Run, Statehood, Dust Bowl caricature, oil derricks, cowboy kitsch or Sonics green and gold
Memorial, 1995 bombing, tornado-damage, Greenwood or 1921 massacre imagery
A rust, crimson-leaning or orange-heavy body that reads as OU, OSU or Texas
Any concept or gradient an earlier Thunder City Edition already used

alternates.name: Deep Deuce

alternates.name: Skydance
alternates.idea: A storm gray-green and Dark Blue set carrying the bridge's sail line, built on sky and never on damage.

alternates.name: Nation-authored edition

partners.name: Plaza District Association
partners.why: Runs Plaza Walls, the Plaza District Festival and the second-Friday LIVE on the Plaza in the city's densest strip of indie shops and murals.
partners.idea: Host a District Series release with a live-painted wall at Plaza Walls 2027.

partners.name: Jabee
partners.why: Long-time voice of Northeast OKC hip-hop and the Black creative scene.
partners.idea: Co-curate the Deep Deuce and Northeast OKC release and its artists for Juneteenth 2027, with proceeds directed by community partners.

partners.name: Greenwood Cultural Center
partners.type: Tulsa Black history and cultural institution
partners.why: The long-standing keeper of Greenwood and Black Wall Street history, and the first call to make before Nike shows up in North Tulsa.
partners.idea: Advise, on paid and credited terms, whether and how the Booker T. Washington program and any Tulsa event happen.

partners.name: First Americans Museum
partners.why: A civic institution that can make introductions but cannot speak for any sovereign nation.
partners.idea: Introductions only, leading to direct agreements with a named nation's cultural or commerce office for the November 2027 program.

partners.name: Yatika Starr Fields
partners.type: Oklahoma muralist and painter (Cherokee, Osage and Muscogee)
partners.why: Internationally exhibited Oklahoma muralist known for bold, color-saturated work.
partners.idea: A paid commission on his own terms, such as a mural or artist piece. He is not a stand-in for any nation.

partners.name: Jeff Chanchaleune (Ma Der Lao Kitchen, Bar Sen)
partners.why: James Beard-recognized chef whose Plaza District restaurants made Lao food an OKC story.
partners.idea: Food pairing at Plaza releases and introductions to Lao community artists. He is not the Asian District anchor.

partners.name: Oklahoma Contemporary Arts Center
partners.why: The state's leading contemporary art venue with studios and a Midtown campus.
partners.idea: Run the open call that selects District Series artists and the City Edition sign painter.

partners.name: Shop Good
partners.why: An N Broadway shop whose Okie-themed goods show what local taste buys.
partners.idea: Stock the Red Dirt capsule and District Series as the tastemaker door Nike lacks in OKC.

risks.risk: Roster churn on a payroll near $260M. Player product also runs through other licensing paths: Gilgeous-Alexander's shoe deal is with Converse, and name-and-number items need NBPA group licensing.
risks.mitigation: Limit names to Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Holmgren in licensed formats, and confirm the brand path for his product. Keep most product team-first. Hold Mara items until his role is clear.

risks.risk: Lead times. New NBA-licensed product takes months, and product built for a deep run sits unsold if the playoffs end early.
risks.mitigation: Use in-line product for October 2026. Put every new line on a spring or August 2027 date, and print round product to demand.

risks.risk: Native appropriation: borrowing the 'Red Earth' name, selling on Statehood Day (the end of Indian Territory) or treating one artist or museum as the voice of the nations.
risks.mitigation: No Statehood Day hooks. Do Native work only under a named nation's written terms, pay and approval, through N7. Support Red Earth only as a paid, credited partner.

risks.risk: Showing up in Tulsa near Greenwood without a local Black partner, or using Black Wall Street or 1921 massacre imagery.
risks.mitigation: No Greenwood, Black Wall Street or massacre imagery. No Tulsa events near May 31 or Juneteenth unless the Greenwood Cultural Center or another named Tulsa Black partner leads.

risks.risk: Thunder product reads as OU crimson, OSU orange or Texas burnt orange and loses half of a split-loyalty household.
risks.mitigation: Keep palettes blue-bodied, with rust and Sunset as trim. Before launch, run fan-panel color reviews in OKC and Tulsa against college gear.

scorecard.rationale: A champion that's the only big-league team in a whole state gives OKC near-top fan intensity and a big statewide opportunity for a small metro. Red dirt, Skydance, Route 66 and community stories give designers plenty to work from. Retail lags: it's a car-based, value-minded market with no Nike community door and a small sneaker scene.
